title: save
summary: Store a command, a piece of history or a multi-line script under a short name.
notes: Saving to a name that exists is an error. Use `-e` to replace it or `-r` to rename it.
Names may contain letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, up to 64 characters. Names with `/` or spaces are refused.
Your quotes and JSON are stored exactly as typed. Wrap the command in quotes so your shell passes it as one value.
Use `%name%` inside a command to make a placeholder. `cwm get` asks for a value when it runs.
Script mode (`-s`) opens your editor and keeps the file in `~/.cwm/scripts/`. Set the editor with `cwm config --editor`.

flags.name: -t, --tag <tags>
flags.desc: Attach tags. One value, comma separated, for example `-t git,util`.

flags.name: -e, --edit
flags.desc: Replace an existing command, or edit an existing script.

flags.name: -r, --rename
flags.desc: Rename an alias. Usage: `cwm save -r old new`.

flags.name: -l, --last
flags.desc: Save the last command from your shell history.

flags.name: -s, --script
flags.desc: Write a multi-line script in your editor. The file lives in `~/.cwm/scripts/`.

examples.title: Save a command with a tag and description
examples.cmd: cwm save hello "echo Hello World" -t util -d "Greets user"
examples.output: Saved [util] hello = echo Hello World (Greets user)

examples.title: Save a command with placeholders
examples.cmd: cwm save deploy "kubectl rollout restart deploy/%name% -n %ns%" -t k8s -d "Restart a deployment"
examples.output: Saved [k8s] deploy = kubectl rollout restart deploy/%name%... (Restart a deployment)

examples.title: Refuse to overwrite
examples.output: Error: Variable 'hello' already exists. (Use -e to edit)
